title: How antibiotics work
examples: Are antibiotics good for everything that makes you sick?
What happens if we take antibiotics when we should not?
How do bacteria actually get sick?

explain.say: Antibiotics are medicines that help fight certain types of germs.
They work by targeting and harming the bacteria that cause infections.
However, antibiotics do not work against viruses, like those causing colds.
A big problem is when bacteria become resistant to these medicines.
If we use them too much, the bacteria can learn to ignore the medicine.

items: Step 1: Taking antibiotics for minor issues

explain.say: In real life, if you get a skin infection, a doctor might prescribe an antibiotic cream.

faq.q: Why do I still get sick even if I take antibiotics?
faq.a: Antibiotics only treat bacterial infections, not all sicknesses. Many common illnesses are caused by viruses, and antibiotics have no effect on viruses.
asks: Why do I need a different medicine?

faq.q: What is antibiotic resistance, and why is it dangerous?
faq.a: Resistance happens when bacteria change and become immune to the medicine. This means the antibiotic will not kill them, making infections much harder to treat.
asks: What does it mean if an antibiotic fails?
Why do we need to be careful with these drugs?

faq.q: Can I just take leftover antibiotics from a previous illness?
faq.a: No, you must take the exact dose prescribed by your doctor for your current infection. Taking old medicine can lead to resistance.
asks: Is it okay to save antibiotics?
How many pills should I take?
Do I need to finish the whole bottle?

faq.q: Are all germs harmful, or are some good?
faq.a: Many bacteria are actually helpful to us, living in our gut for digestion. However, some types can cause harmful infections.

faq.q: How long does it take for antibiotics to start working?
faq.a: The medicine usually starts working relatively quickly, but it takes time for the full course of treatment to clear the infection completely. It is important to finish the entire prescription.
asks: Should I stop taking it early?

facts: Antibiotics are designed to kill or stop the growth of bacteria.
They have no effect on viruses, such as those that cause the common cold.
Overusing antibiotics can lead to antibiotic resistance in bacteria.
Doctors prescribe antibiotics only when a bacterial infection is suspected.

quiz.say: Antibiotics are effective against which type of germ?
quiz.why: Antibiotics specifically target the structures found in bacterial cells to stop them from reproducing.

wrong.0: Viruses are much smaller and replicate inside cells, which antibiotics do not target.
wrong.1: Fungi require different types of medicines, called antifungals, to be treated.
wrong.2: Toxins are substances, not living germs, so antibiotics have nothing to act upon.

quiz.say: What is the main danger of using antibiotics when you do not need them?
quiz.why: When bacteria are not challenged by antibiotics, they are not forced to become stronger, which helps prevent resistance.

wrong.0: Overgrowth is a possible side effect, but resistance is the major public health concern.
wrong.2: Immunity is the body's natural defense, and antibiotics do not build this up.
wrong.3: Toxicity refers to poison, which is not the main risk of overuse.

quiz.say: If a person has a cold, the doctor might suggest rest and fluids. This is because:

options.show: The medicine will help the body fight the virus.
options.say: The medicine will help the body fight the virus.

options.show: They need antibiotics to kill the germs.
options.say: They need antibiotics to kill the germs.

options.show: Rest helps the body build natural immunity.
options.say: Rest helps the body build natural immunity.

quiz.why: Since antibiotics only fight bacteria, they cannot treat a cold which is caused by a virus.

wrong.0: Antibiotics are not designed to help the body fight viruses.
wrong.2: This assumes the cold is bacterial, which is incorrect.
wrong.3: While rest is good, this option misses the key scientific point about the virus.
